newsitem.title: RUSSIA: LUKoil looks to stay top of Russia's oil pack.
newsitem.headline: LUKoil looks to stay top of Russia's oil pack.

text.p: Russia's biggest oil company, LUKoil, consolidated its position at the head of the country's dozen or so vertically-integrated oil companies last year, showing strong profit growth and rising oil production.

LUKoil president Vagit Alekperov told the annual shareholders meeting on Thursday that 1996 was the best performance by the group in three years, but major investments were needed in 1997 to sustain growth in all sectors.
"Last year were the best production and financial results we have had in the last three years," he said. "In 1996 LUKoil showed clearly it was the strongest oil company in Russia."
LUKoil's main objective for the future was to boost oil production, the company's annual report said.
Alekperov said LUKoil's main achievements was to boost oil production last year.

It produced 58.5 million tonnes of oil (1.17 million barrels per day), up two percent from 57.3 million (1.15 million bpd) in 1995. LUKoil plans to boost output further to around 59.7 million tonnes (1.19 million bpd) this year.
The report also said the firm could boost output annually by seven million tonnes (140,000 bpd) by 2000 through technological improvements.
The company has been much more aggressive than its Russian rivals in boosting its portfolio outside Russia, where high production and transport costs have made oil output expensive.
LUKoil has already signed large production deals in Iraq and Kazakhstan, and is part of a consortium building a major new pipeline from Kazakhstan to the Black Sea.
The company's annual report said last year it continued preliminary work on production projects in Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Tunisia and Egypt.
Production outside Russia last year accounted for only half of one percent of the company's total output, but this share is expected to grow.

"LUKoil is looking to increase the share of international operations in the oil and oil product sectors, and is broadening participation in opening highly productive oil and gas fields abroad," Alekperov said in a written address to shareholders.
As output rises, LUKoil wants to boost the amount of proven oil reserves it holds.
"Last year we were actively looking to increase our oil reserves. We are already looking at countries like Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan and Iraq," Alekperov said.
The company already says it is the world's largest private oil company in terms of reserves, owning an estimated 10.5 billion barrels in Russia alone.
LUKoil boosted reserves by 65.3 million tonnes in 1996 and 64.7 million in 1995, 12 percent and 13 percent above production levels respectively.
The third thrust to LUKoil's development plan is to raise the volumes and quality of oil products it produces and exports.
"We want to increase exports of our oil products and to improve the quality," Alekperov said.
LUKoil expects to boost refining to 19.8 million tonnes (396,000 bpd) in 1997, up two percent from 19.3 million tonnes (386,000 bpd) it refined in 1996.
It also wants to export 6.0 million tonnes of products this year, up a third from 1996 deliveries of 4.5 million tonnes.
The company plans to boost product output through acquiring new refining capacity in Russia and Commonwealth of Independent States countries and upgrading existing facilities, the annual report said.
